trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out down or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Number 2 is only reachable this way.
Going to number 3, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going up would force the line onto number 13 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Number 3 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
Going down would strand number 4: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going right would force the line onto number 10 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Going right would strand number 7: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Number 9 is only reachable this way.
The line must go down: up is number 12, which comes later; right is number 11, which comes later.
Going right would force the line onto number 11 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Cell (6,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Cell (1,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going left would leave both cell (1,3) and cell (2,4) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
